definitions.explanation: A short pin with a flat, broad head used to fasten papers or posters to a board or wall.

examples.japanese: {画鋲|がびょう}でポスターを{貼|は}った。
examples.english: I pinned up the poster with thumbtacks.

examples.japanese: {床|ゆか}に{落|お}ちていた{画鋲|がびょう}を{踏|ふ}んでしまった。
examples.english: I accidentally stepped on a thumbtack that had fallen on the floor.

examples.japanese: {掲示板|けいじばん}に{画鋲|がびょう}で{連絡|れんらく}{事項|じこう}を{留|と}めてください。
examples.english: Please pin the notices to the bulletin board with thumbtacks.

notes:
Combines {画|が} (picture/drawing) and {鋲|びょう} (tack/rivet). Originally used to pin drawings and documents, the name persists even though thumbtacks are now used for many purposes.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {画鋲|がびょう}で{留|と}める: fasten with a thumbtack
- {画鋲|がびょう}で{貼|は}る: pin up with thumbtacks
- {画鋲|がびょう}を{刺|さ}す: stick in a thumbtack
- {画鋲|がびょう}を{抜|ぬ}く: pull out a thumbtack
- {画鋲|がびょう}を{踏|ふ}む: step on a thumbtack

USAGE:
A common everyday word learned early in school life. Japanese classrooms typically use {画鋲|がびょう} to attach items to cork bulletin boards ({掲示板|けいじばん}). The word is universally understood across Japan, though some regions may use the older reading {押|お}しピン.

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ピン: pin — a more general loanword; can refer to various types of pins
- {押|お}しピン: pushpin — dialectal variant (mainly Kansai region) for the same item
